turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you holding up?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My book club gets to pick next month's book and it's my turn to choose.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm going to list all the options first, so please don't comment until I'm done.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The first one is a long fantasy novel, about eight hundred pages, with dragons and a huge cast.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then there's a short memoir about a woman who sailed around the world by herself.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Option three is a mystery set in a small fishing town, the kind you can't put down.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the last one is a book about the history of salt, which sounds odd but has great reviews.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Eight hundred pages is a lot for a month, so the fantasy novel might lose half the club. The mystery is a safe choice, easy to read and fun to discuss who did it. The sailing memoir is short and inspiring, which could spark a nice conversation.
